newsitem.title: USA: McTeer speech intended to emphasize 1996 economy.
newsitem.headline: McTeer speech intended to emphasize 1996 economy.

text.p: A speech Tuesday by Dallas Fed President Robert McTeer was intended to emphasize the economic conditions in 1996, not describe the stance of monetary policy in 1997, according to Harvey Rosenblum, the bank's research director.
"I spoke to him after the speech," Rosenblum told Reuters, "He thought he had been quoted a little bit out of context."
Rosenblum was referring to a news agency report that quoted McTeer as suggesting that the Fed was not ready to raise interest rates yet.
According to the report, the Dallas Fed chief told a luncheon, "We're on guard but there's nothing to tip us over into tightening."
Reuters did not attend the luncheon.
Rosenblum said McTeer was "reiterating what was going on in 1996," saying that the forces in the economy "tended to cancel each other out."
He added that McTeer had not been trying to make a point about monetary policy in 1997 or "tip his hand" ahead of the upcoming March 25 Federal Open Market Committee Meeting.
